summary: A password field with a Show password toggle. The toggle keeps its name and says its state with `aria-pressed`, and a polite status says "Password shown" or "Password hidden". A shown password is never spellchecked, and is hidden again before its form is submitted.
useWhen: the user types a password, a passphrase or a PIN they must get right without seeing it
signing in, signing up, changing a password, or confirming one before a sensitive action

useInstead.when: the secret is shown once for the user to copy — a new API key
useInstead.why: it is shown on purpose, in full, with a copy button; masking it and then offering to show it adds a step and nothing else

useInstead.when: a one-time code sent by text or email
useInstead.why: a one-time code is read off another screen and typed; masking it only makes it harder to check. Use `inputMode="numeric"` and `autoComplete="one-time-code"`

composition.note: Takes Input's `label`, `description`, `isInvalid` and `errorMessage`. `autoComplete` is `current-password` by default; pass `new-password` where one is being set.
composition.example: <PasswordInput label="New password" autoComplete="new-password" description="At least 12 characters." />

requires: `label` — a visible one; a placeholder is not a label
guarantees: the toggle is a tab stop after the field, named `revealLabel` ("Show password") whatever the state; `aria-pressed` says whether the password is shown, and `aria-controls` points at the field
a polite status says `shownMessage` or `hiddenMessage` when the toggle changes it, and nothing on first render
a mouse press on the toggle leaves focus in the field; a keyboard press leaves it on the toggle; what was typed and the caret's place are kept
spellcheck, autocorrect and autocapitalise are off, shown or hidden, and cannot be turned back on by a prop
submitting the form hides the password before the form's own handler runs, so a password manager sees `type="password"`
`autoComplete` is `current-password` unless set; `new-password` lets a password manager offer to generate one
`isDisabled` disables the toggle too; `isReadOnly` leaves it working
the box is Input's, with Input's sizes and states
notes: do not block paste into a password field: it breaks password managers, and WCAG 3.3.8 counts it against an accessible sign-in
state the rules before the user types — "At least 12 characters" in `description` — rather than only in the error after

antiPatterns.dont: <Input type="password" trailingIcon={<Eye />} /> with an onClick on the icon
antiPatterns.why: an icon is not a button: it cannot be focused or pressed from the keyboard, is not announced, and the shown password is spellchecked

antiPatterns.dont: a toggle whose name flips between "Show password" and "Hide password"
antiPatterns.why: a screen reader reads a changed name as a different control, and the user cannot tell whether the press worked

antiPatterns.dont: a "Confirm password" field under a new-password field
antiPatterns.do: one PasswordInput the user can show
antiPatterns.why: typing a password twice blind catches fewer mistakes than seeing it once, and costs every user a field
